intro: NASA's SPHEREx telescope photographs the whole sky again and again. Stars stay put. Asteroids, comets and maybe a hidden planet move. Watch two real scans flicker and tap anything that jumps.
loadError: The scans didn't load. Check your connection and reload the page.
hint: Tap the dot that jumps between Scan A and Scan B.
hintMore: {n} more mover to find in this field.
miss: Not a known mover. It could be a star that changed brightness, a cosmic ray, or something new.
noneRightTxt: No known mover is bright enough to see here. Ruling out patches of sky like this is how the Planet X search narrows down.
noneWrongTxt: There was a mover in this field. It's circled now.
badgeSim: Simulated object on a real SPHEREx image
simTxt: The game planted this dot to train your eye. Real asteroids look just like it.
skyTxt: Every empty patch you check narrows where a Planet X could hide. SPHEREx maps the whole sky, about 41,000 square degrees, every six months.
credit: SPHEREx images: NASA/JPL-Caltech via NASA/IPAC IRSA. Asteroid positions: IMCCE SkyBoT and JPL Horizons. Facts: JPL Small-Body Database.
